ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, $AB = 6$, and $E$ is the midpoint of $BC$. $AE$ and $BD$ intersect at point $F$. Connect $CF$. If $AE \perp BD$, what is the length of $CF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, draw $FM\perp BC$ through point F, with FM intersecting BC at point M\\
$\because$ rectangle ABCD\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABE=\angle BAD=\angle ACD=90^\circ$, $BC=AD$\\
$\because$AE$\perp$BD\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAF+\angle ABF=\angle ADB+\angle ABF=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAF=\angle ADB$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BAD\sim \triangle EBA$\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{AB}{BE}$\\
$\because$E is the midpoint of BC\\
$\therefore$ $AD=BC=2BE$\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{2BE}{6}=\frac{6}{BE}$\\
$\therefore$ $2BE^2=36$\\
$\therefore$ $BE=\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt{2}$\\
Upon verification, $BE\ne 0$, it is a solution to the original equation $\frac{2BE}{6}=\frac{6}{BE}$\\
$\therefore$ $AD=BC=2BE=6\sqrt{2}$\\
$\therefore$ $BD=\sqrt{AB^2+AD^2}=6\sqrt{3}$, $AE=\sqrt{AB^2+BE^2}=3\sqrt{6}$\\
$\therefore$ $BF=\frac{AB\times BE}{AE}=\frac{6\times 3\sqrt{2}}{3\sqrt{6}}=2\sqrt{3}$\\
$\because$ $\angle FBE=\angle CBD$, $\angle BFE=\angle ACD=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BFE\sim \triangle BCD$\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{FM}{CD}=\frac{BF}{BD}$\\
$\therefore$ $FM=\frac{CD\times BF}{BD}=\frac{6\times 2\sqrt{3}}{6\sqrt{3}}=2$\\
$\therefore$ $BM=\sqrt{BF^2−FM^2}=\sqrt{12−4}=2\sqrt{2}$\\
$\therefore$ $CM=BC−BM=6\sqrt{2}−2\sqrt{2}=4\sqrt{2}$\\
$\therefore$ $FC=\sqrt{FM^2+CM^2}=\sqrt{4+32}=\boxed{6}$

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, $AB = 6$, and $E$ is the midpoint of $BC$. $AE$ and $BD$ intersect at point $F$. Connect $CF$. If $AE \perp BD$, what is the length of $CF$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, draw $FM\perp BC$ through point F, with FM intersecting BC at point M\\
$\because$ rectangle ABCD\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABE=\angle BAD=\angle ACD=90^\circ$, $BC=AD$\\
$\because$AE$\perp$BD\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAF+\angle ABF=\angle ADB+\angle ABF=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAF=\angle ADB$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BAD\sim \triangle EBA$\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{AB}{BE}$\\
$\because$E is the midpoint of BC\\
$\therefore$ $AD=BC=2BE$\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{2BE}{6}=\frac{6}{BE}$\\
$\therefore$ $2BE^2=36$\\
$\therefore$ $BE=\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt{2}$\\
Upon verification, $BE\ne 0$, it is a solution to the original equation $\frac{2BE}{6}=\frac{6}{BE}$\\
$\therefore$ $AD=BC=2BE=6\sqrt{2}$\\
$\therefore$ $BD=\sqrt{AB^2+AD^2}=6\sqrt{3}$, $AE=\sqrt{AB^2+BE^2}=3\sqrt{6}$\\
$\therefore$ $BF=\frac{AB\times BE}{AE}=\frac{6\times 3\sqrt{2}}{3\sqrt{6}}=2\sqrt{3}$\\
$\because$ $\angle FBE=\angle CBD$, $\angle BFE=\angle ACD=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BFE\sim \triangle BCD$\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{FM}{CD}=\frac{BF}{BD}$\\
$\therefore$ $FM=\frac{CD\times BF}{BD}=\frac{6\times 2\sqrt{3}}{6\sqrt{3}}=2$\\
$\therefore$ $BM=\sqrt{BF^2−FM^2}=\sqrt{12−4}=2\sqrt{2}$\\
$\therefore$ $CM=BC−BM=6\sqrt{2}−2\sqrt{2}=4\sqrt{2}$\\
$\therefore$ $FC=\sqrt{FM^2+CM^2}=\sqrt{4+32}=\boxed{6}$

claims.source: According to analytic geometry, set B=(0,0), A=(0,6), C=(w,0), D=(w,6).

claims.claim: E is the midpoint of BC.
claims.label: perception
claims.source: Because E is the midpoint of BC

claims.claim: Vector BD=(w,6).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Vector BD=(w,6)

claims.claim: The dot product of perpendicular vectors is 0.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: AE⊥BD, the dot product is 0

claims.claim: AE⊥BD。
claims.label: perception
claims.source: From AE⊥BD

claims.claim: Since F is on BD and AE, F can be set as F=t(w,6), and at the same time F=(0,6)+s(w/2,-6).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Let F be on BD, then F=t(w,6); at the same time F is on AE, then F=(0,6)+s(w/2,-6).

claims.claim: Compare coordinates and solve to get t=1/3.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Compare coordinates: tw=sw/2, 6t=6-6s. From the first equation s=2t, substitute into the second equation to get t=1-2t, so t=1/3.

claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore F=(w/3,2)

claims.claim: The distance between two points can be calculated by taking the square root of the sum of the squares of the coordinate differences.
claims.label: knowledge

claims.claim: Substitute C=(w,0), F=(w/3,2), and w=6√2 to get CF=6.
claims.label: reasoning
